title: Subtract Two Linked List Numbers
description:
You are given two non-empty singly linked lists `l1` and `l2` representing two non-negative integers with the **most significant digit** at the head of each list (neither number contains leading zeros except when representing `0` itself).

Return a singly linked list representing the absolute difference `|num(l1) - num(l2)|` with the most significant digit at the head and no unnecessary leading zeros. If both numbers are equal, return a single node with value `0`.
constraints: The number of nodes in each list is in the range [1, 10^4].
Neither input list has leading zeros except for the single-node list [0].
hints: First compare the magnitudes of `l1` and `l2` (longer list is larger; on equal lengths compare digit-by-digit from head) so you always subtract the smaller number from the larger one.
Reverse both lists, perform schoolbook subtraction from least significant digit with a borrow flag, reverse the resulting list, and strip any leading zero nodes (leaving at least one node).
